keywords: distinguishing language errors from application failures
subtopics: Distinguishing language errors from application failures.
learning_outcomes: Explain what understanding php errors contributes to a PHP application.
Apply at least one of these concepts in a small example: parse errors.
Check one edge case and explain how to diagnose unexpected behavior.

content.intro: Failures need an explicit policy. Exceptions should propagate to a layer that can handle them, while logs preserve useful diagnostics without exposing internal details to users. In this lesson, focus on parse errors; then compare it with runtime errors. Use the example to predict a result before checking it, and record one case where the behavior may differ.
content.why_it_matters: You will use understanding php errors when building readable, testable PHP programs. Its practical value is knowing which rule applies, what result to expect, and how to handle failure or unexpected input.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Failures need an explicit policy. Exceptions should propagate to a layer that can handle them, while logs preserve useful diagnostics without exposing internal details to users. For understanding php errors, begin with parse errors. Also distinguish runtime errors; warnings and notices; type errors. Identify the input, the rule applied, and the observable output or side effect; then check the relevant official reference when a version or edge-case detail matters.

content_blocks.title: A small PHP example for Understanding PHP Errors
content_blocks.code:
<?php
try { throw new RuntimeException("Example failure"); } catch (RuntimeException $error) { echo "Handled" . PHP_EOL; }

common_mistakes.problem: Copying a pattern without understanding its inputs and output.
common_mistakes.why: Small environment or type differences can change behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Trace one example by hand, name expected outputs, and consult version-matched official docs.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring empty, invalid, or boundary input.
common_mistakes.why: Real data rarely matches only the simplest example.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a deliberate edge-case check before relying on the result.

common_mistakes.problem: Making several changes at once while debugging.
common_mistakes.why: It becomes difficult to identify which change caused the behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Reduce the issue to one small reproducible case, change one cause, and retest.
